Roentgenium (German: [ʁœntˈɡeːni̯ʊm]) is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Rg and atomic number 111.
What is the atomic number of Mercury?
Mercury is a chemical element; it has symbol Hg and atomic number 80.
In what year did Josef Mengele die?
Josef Mengele: Before the war, Mengele received doctorates in anthropology and medicine, and he began a career as a researcher.
In what year was Carbon discovered?
Carbon (from Latin carbo 'coal') is a chemical element; it has symbol C and atomic number 6.
Which company manufactures Boeing AH-64 Apache?
Boeing AH-64 Apache: Hughes Helicopters. The Apache began as the Model 77 developed by Hughes Helicopters for the United States Army's Advanced Attack Helicopter program to replace the AH-1 Cobra.
Rendang: Indonesia. It refers to both a cooking method of frying and the dish cooked in that way.
Who is credited with discovering Circinus?
Circinus: Nicolas Louis de Lacaille. Circinus is a small, faint constellation in the southern sky, first defined in 1756 by the French astronomer Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille.
Who is credited with discovering Citric acid?
Citric acid: Carl Wilhelm Scheele. Citric acid is an organic compound with the formula C6H8O7.
Who is credited with discovering Helium?
Helium: Pierre Janssen. Helium (from Ancient Greek: ἥλιος, romanized: helios, lit. 'sun') is a chemical element; it has symbol He and atomic number 2.
Russell Crowe stars in this 2001 Ron Howard film about a Nobel Prize-winning mathematician's struggle with schizophrenia, based on Sylvia Nasar's biography. What's the title?
A Beautiful Mind (film) is a 2001 American biographical drama film about the mathematician John Nash who won a Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences.
Which diverse group of aquatic photosynthetic organisms excludes land plants but includes seaweeds that can grow up to 50 metres long?
Algae (UK also; sing.: alga) are any of a large and diverse group of photosynthetic organisms.

Its name means 'unlike other shrimp.' Known best from the Burgess Shale, this extinct radiodont swam with body flaps and stared out through huge compound eyes packed with lenses — what was this stem-arthropod?

Anomalocaris (from Ancient Greek, meaning "anomalous", and, meaning "shrimp", with the intended meaning "unlike other shrimp") is an extinct genus of radiodont, an order of early-diverging stem-group marine arthropods.
A methyl ester built from aspartic acid and phenylalanine, this non-saccharide sweetener is among the most-studied food additives ever, judged safe by over 100 regulatory bodies — what is it?
Aspartame is an artificial, non-saccharide sweetener commonly used as a sugar substitute in foods and beverages.
Recorded in an ancient Chinese herbal medicine text from around 200 BC and named for a barberry-related plant genus, this yellow-pigmented alkaloid glows under ultraviolet light. What compound is it?
Berberine is an organic compound classified as benzylisoquinoline alkaloid.
Accepted by the American Kennel Club in 1893, this small, compact dog breed with a short tail and erect ears originated in the United States — name the breed?
Boston Terrier is a breed of dog originating in the United States of America.
Its common name is a contraction of 'Mary's gold,' honoring the Virgin Mary, but this daisy-family genus's Latin name nods to the calendar instead — which flowering plant?
Calendula is a genus of about 15-20 species of annual and perennial herbaceous plants in the daisy family, Asteraceae that are often known as marigolds.
This worldwide family of over 5,000 fly species — found everywhere except the Antarctic and Arctic — includes the biting midges also known as sand flies — what is it called?
Ceratopogonidae is a family of flies colloquially known as no-see-ums, sand flies, or biting midges, generally 1-3 millimetres (116-18 in) in length.
This anatomical term for the hollow between a woman's breasts was coined in its modern sense by a Hollywood censor reviewing the 1943 film starring Jane Russell — what is the term?
Cleavage (breasts) is the narrow depression or hollow between the breasts of a woman.
Made up of subregions called the genu, rostrum, trunk, and splenium, this thick nerve tract lets the brain's two hemispheres communicate — what is it?
Corpus callosum (Latin for "tough body"), also callosal commissure, is a wide, thick nerve tract, consisting of a flat bundle of commissural fibers, beneath the cerebral cortex in the brain.
This computer scientist, who died in October 2011, partnered with Ken Thompson to build Unix and also devised the C and B programming languages — who is he?
Covering everything from a fibrous bone condition to a kidney disorder, this term for abnormal tissue growth is usually precancerous rather than outright malignant — what is it?

Dysplasia is any of various types of abnormal growth or development of cells (microscopic scale) or organs (macroscopic scale), and the abnormal histology or anatomical structure(s) resulting from such growth.

This is the only living group of horses, asses, and zebras — odd-toed, herbivorous mammals whose ancestors first evolved in North America before spreading into Asia, Africa, and South America — what is it?
Equus (genus) is a genus of mammals in the perissodactyl family Equidae, which includes horses, asses, and zebras.

First recognised in the 1950s but not formally defined until 1990, this disorder of widespread chronic pain — often with fatigue and memory trouble — has no known cause and is treated multidisciplinarily. What is it?
Fibromyalgia (FM) is a long-term condition characterised by widespread chronic pain.

This inflammation of the stomach lining is commonly caused by H. pylori infection or NSAID use, and can lead to complications like ulcers or, in its autoimmune form, pernicious anemia — what condition is it?
Gastritis is the inflammation of the lining of the stomach. It may occur as a short episode or have a long duration.
Designed in the late 1950s as a replacement for the piston-engined E-1 Tracer, this twin-turboprop U.S. Navy aircraft provides carrier-based early warning radar coverage. Name the aircraft?
Grumman E-2 Hawkeye is an American all-weather, carrier-capable, tactical airborne early warning (AEW) aircraft.

Fox-sized and found on every continent but Australia and Antarctica, these primitive ornithischian dinosaurs are known for odd teeth — canine-like tusks plus cheek teeth built for chewing. What's this family?
Heterodontosauridae is a family of ornithischian dinosaurs that were likely among the most basal (primitive) members of the group.
This birth defect, found in roughly one in every 250 newborn boys, involves an opening that fails to form in its typical location — what condition is this?

Hypospadias is a common malformation in fetal development, most commonly noticed in penises, in which the urethra does not open from its usual location on the head of the penis, or the middle of the vulva.
A pioneer of radio microwave optics who also wrote science fiction and has a lunar crater named for him, this Indian polymath founded Asia's first interdisciplinary research institute — who was he?
Jagadish Chandra Bose (30 November 1858 - 23 November 1937) was an Indian polymath with interests in biology, physics and writing science fiction.
Honored across Asia as a model healer and "Medicine King," this 5th-century BCE physician of Rajgir tended to King Bimbisāra — and to the Buddha himself. Who was he?
Jīvaka was the personal physician of the Buddha and the Indian King Bimbisra.
Closely related to earthworms but equipped with a sucker at each end, these segmented parasitic or predatory worms make up their own subclass within the annelid phylum — what are they?
Leech are segmented parasitic or predatory worms that comprise the subclass Hirudinea within the phylum Annelida.

Ranging across Eurasia with plumage of black, white, pink, and grey, this small insectivorous bird forms compact family flocks of six to seventeen outside the breeding season, its northern subspecies sporting all-white heads — which bird?
Long-tailed tit (Aegithalos caudatus) is a common bird species belonging to the bushtit family found throughout Eurasia.

Dubbed "sea locusts" by the ancient Assyrians and "prawn killers" elsewhere, these burrow-dwelling marine crustaceans are among the top predators of tropical shallows — yet they remain poorly understood. What are they?
Mantis shrimp are carnivorous marine crustaceans of the order Stomatopoda (from Ancient Greek (stma) 'mouth' and (pos) 'foot').
This field's founding body, the Bureau International des Poids et Mesures, grew out of an 1875 convention and eventually gave the world the International System of Units — what is this study called?
Metrology is the scientific study of measurement.
An Austrian-School economist who called the state 'robbery systematized and writ large,' he founded and championed anarcho-capitalism across more than twenty books — who was he?
Murray Rothbard (March 2, 1926 - January 7, 1995) was an American economist of the Austrian School, economic historian, political theorist, and activist.

First described in 1766 by naturalist Peter Simon Pallas, this sole living member of its genus sports a white throat patch and, in males only, a pair of short horns — what is this large Asian antelope called?
Nilgai (Boselaphus tragocamelus) (literally meaning "blue cow") is the largest antelope in Asia.
Found on every continent except Antarctica, this fish-eating raptor nests near water and can be identified by its brown back and pale, grayish head — what bird is it?
Osprey (Pandion haliaetus), historically known as sea hawk, river hawk, and fish hawk, is a diurnal, fish-eating bird of prey with a cosmopolitan range.
Innervated by two dedicated nerves and inserting near the upper arm's bicipital groove, which broad chest muscle flexes and internally rotates the humerus?
Pectoralis major (from Latin pectus 'breast') is a thick, fan-shaped or triangular convergent muscle of the human chest.
This French physicist shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics with his wife, making them the first married couple ever to win a Nobel — who is he?
Pierre Curie (15 May 1859 - 19 April 1906) was a French physicist and chemist, and a pioneer in crystallography and magnetism.
Used to disinfect both healthcare workers' hands and patients' skin before and after surgery, this antiseptic can be applied as a liquid, ointment, or powder — which compound?

Povidone-iodine is an antiseptic used for skin disinfection before and after surgery. Povidone-iodine (PVP-I), also known as iodopovidone, is an antiseptic used for skin disinfection before and after surgery.
The sole member of the genus Setonix, this cat-sized, mainly nocturnal Australian marsupial famously inhabits Rottnest Island — what is it?
Quokka (Setonix brachyurus) is a small macropod about the size of a domestic cat.

This English mathematical physicist shared a 1988 Wolf Prize with Stephen Hawking, won a 2020 Nobel for black-hole work, and dreamed up an 'impossible' triangle that inspired M. C. Escher — who is he?
Roger Penrose (born 8 August 1931) is an English mathematician, mathematical physicist, and philosopher of science.
Developed by the MIT Media Lab for children ages 5 to 16, this block-based visual programming language and website has been translated into more than 70 languages — name it?
Scratch (programming language) is a high-level, block-based visual programming language and website aimed primarily at children as an educational tool, with a target audience of ages 5 to 16.
This group of nocturnal Southeast Asian primates ranges from Yunnan province in China down to the island of Java, with a pygmy relative recently reclassified into its own genus — what are they?
Slow loris are a group of several species of nocturnal strepsirrhine primates that make up the genus Nycticebus.
Built from four fused rings, compounds in this class include cholesterol, testosterone, and anti-inflammatory drugs like dexamethasone. What class of compound is it?
Steroid is an organic compound with four fused rings (designated A, B, C, and D) arranged in a specific molecular configuration.
Symbol Tc, atomic number 43: this silvery-gray metal is entirely synthetic, though tiny natural traces form via neutron capture in molybdenum ore — what element?
Technetium is a chemical element; it has symbol Tc and atomic number 43.
This metric unit of mass equals exactly 1,000 kilograms — about 2,204.6 pounds — and is technically identical to the SI unit called the megagram. What is it?
Tonne (or; symbol: t) is a unit of mass equal to 1,000 kilograms.

First identified in 1801 by a Spanish-Mexican scientist analyzing a mineral he dubbed 'brown lead,' this hard, silvery-grey transition metal carries atomic number 23 and chemical symbol V — what's the element?
Vanadium is a chemical element; it has symbol V and atomic number 23.
The largest land-dwelling member of the weasel family, this solitary, muscular carnivore of the northern boreal forests can kill prey far larger than itself — what animal is it?
Wolverine (US also; Gulo gulo), also called the carcajou or quickhatch (from East Cree, kwiihkwahaacheew), is the largest land-dwelling member of the family Mustelidae.
Accidentally discovered in 1967 by German chemist Karl Clauss at Hoechst AG, which calorie-free artificial sweetener is sold under the brand names Sunett and Sweet One?

Designed to replace the Lockheed C-130 Hercules and sized between it and the Boeing C-17, this four-engine European turboprop military transporter first flew from Seville in December 2009 despite nearly being cancelled over cost overruns. What's the aircraft?
Airbus A400M Atlas: Multi-national four-engine turboprop military transport aircraft.
A striking red-capped, white-warted mushroom of northern forests, this fungus may owe its name to an old use against flies — or to a medieval belief that flies caused madness. What is it?
Amanita muscaria: Species of mushroom. Amanita muscaria, commonly known as the fly agaric or fly amanita, is a basidiomycete fungus of the genus Amanita.

Multicellular eukaryotes that breathe oxygen and grow from a hollow ball of cells called a blastula, over 1.5 million species in this kingdom have been described by scientists. What are they collectively called?
Animal: Biological kingdom. Over 1.5 million living animal species have been described, of which around 1.05 million are insects, over 85,000 are molluscs, and around 65,000 are vertebrates.
The clinging seed burrs of this plant genus, commonly known as burdock, directly inspired the invention of the hook-and-loop fastener — which genus?
This British mathematician and logician coined the phrase 'mathematical induction' and gave his name to a pair of laws relating conjunction, disjunction, and negation. Who was he?
Augustus De Morgan: British mathematician and logician (1806–1871)
Produced continuously from 1964 to 2021, this line of twin-turboprop utility aircraft outsold all of its turboprop rivals combined — which aircraft family?
Beechcraft King Air: Twin engine turboprop aircraft family. The King Air line comprises a number of twin-turboprop models that have been divided into two families.
Not a species of its own, it's really a melanistic leopard or jaguar whose rosettes are still hidden under the dark coat — what do we call this big-cat colour variant?
Black panther: Variant of leopard and jaguar. Black panthers of both species have excess black pigments, but their typical rosettes are also present.
This subfamily of horned, cloven-hooved ungulates includes cattle, bison, and both African and water buffalo, with the gaur as its largest living member — which group?
Jointly developed by Pakistan and China as a lightweight fourth-generation fighter meant to eventually succeed the F-16 in Pakistan's air force, this jet's Chinese designation is FC-1 — what is it?
CAC/PAC JF-17 Thunder: Sino-Pakistani multirole fighter aircraft.
With the formula H2CO3, this fleeting compound has a lifespan of only about 20 milliseconds at body temperature before converting to water and carbon dioxide — which compound?
Carbonic acid: Chemical compound. The molecule rapidly converts to water and carbon dioxide in the presence of water.
Discovered in 1945 and first sold in 1964, this class of beta-lactam antibiotics was originally pulled from a fungus once known as Cephalosporium — what's the family called?
This form of cancer that begins in the tubes carrying digestive fluid from the liver can cause yellowing skin, dark urine, and pale stools — what is it?
Cholangiocarcinoma: Cancer of the bile ducts.
Commonly called the tailbone, this bone is the vestigial remnant of a tail in humans and other tailless primates, sitting just below the sacrum — which bone?
Coccyx: Bone of the pelvis. In tailless primates (e.g. humans and other great apes) since Nacholapithecus (a Miocene hominoid), the coccyx is the remnant of a vestigial tail.
First created near Darmstadt in 1996 and named for an astronomer on his 537th anniversary, this synthetic element (number 112) is so volatile it may even be a gas — which element?
Copernicium: Chemical element with atomic number 112 (Cn)
Sold under trade names like Super Glue and Krazy Glue, this fast-acting adhesive family rapidly polymerizes the moment it contacts water — which chemical group?
Cyanoacrylate: Type of fast-acting adhesive. The cyanoacrylate group in the monomer rapidly polymerizes in the presence of water to form long, strong chains.
With evidence of practice dating back to 7000 BC, this field is considered the very first specialization to branch off from general medicine — what is it?
Dentistry: Branch of medicine. Dentistry, also known as dental medicine and oral medicine, is the branch of medicine focused on the teeth, gums, and mouth.
Nicknamed 'Spad' after a World War I fighter, this piston-engine attack plane flew from 1946 into the 1980s, an anachronism deep into the Jet Age — which aircraft?
Douglas A-1 Skyraider: American single engine attack aircraft.
Linked with orgasm and involving involuntary pelvic-floor contractions, this male bodily process can even happen during sleep as a so-called 'wet dream' — what is it?
Ejaculation: Semen discharge from the male reproductive tract.
This 1939 Nobel Physics laureate invented the cyclotron and went on to found two national laboratories that carry his surname today — who was he?

Scientifically known as Chloris chloris, this small finch is widespread across Europe, North Africa, and Southwest Asia, and has also been introduced to Australia, New Zealand, Uruguay, and Argentina — what bird is this?
European greenfinch: Species of bird. The European greenfinch or simply the greenfinch (Chloris chloris) is a small passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae.
Historically used in the 18th century to track down escaped slaves, this large Brazilian dog breed of mastiff type now also serves as a guard dog and companion — which breed?
Fila Brasileiro: Brazilian breed of dog. The Fila Brasileiro (Portuguese pronunciation: [ˈfilɐ bɾaziˈlejɾu]) is a Brazilian breed of large working dog of mastiff type.

Coated in cornmeal and pan-cooked while still unripe, this dish was originally a Northeastern and Midwestern staple before a hit movie rebranded it as quintessentially Southern comfort food — what is it?
Fried green tomatoes: American dish. Fried green tomatoes is a culinary dish usually found in the United States, made from unripe (green) tomatoes coated with cornmeal and fried.

Working at Tuskegee Institute, this agricultural scientist urged cotton farmers to plant peanuts and sweet potatoes instead, publishing dozens of practical bulletins to fight soil depletion. Who is he?
George Washington Carver: American botanist and inventor (1864–1943)
Credited alongside Isaac Newton with inventing calculus, this German polymath also pioneered binary arithmetic and earned the nickname 'the last universal genius' — who is he?
Nicknamed the slime eel, this jawless marine scavenger is the only living animal with a skull but no proper backbone — what is it?
Hagfish: Class of eel-shaped, slime-producing animal.
This German-American statistician patented an electromechanical punched-card tabulating machine in 1884, founding a company that would eventually be renamed IBM — who was he?
Herman Hollerith: American statistician and inventor. Hollerith founded a company that was amalgamated in 1911 with several other companies to form the Computing-Tabulating-Recording Company.
This climbing, hemp-family plant's female cone-shaped flowers are used to flavor and preserve beer — what's the scientific name for hops?
Humulus lupulus: Species of flowering plant.
Formed by the merger of two hip flexor muscles that join at the femur's lesser trochanter, this is the body's strongest flexor of the hip — what is it called?
Iliopsoas: Joined psoas and iliacus muscles of the hip and thigh.
This tech entrepreneur co-founded Twitter, later built a fintech company behind Square, Cash App, and Tidal, and also helped launch the decentralized network Bluesky?
As a Princeton grad student this mathematician dreamed up an "equilibrium" concept that won him a 1994 Nobel in Economics — who was he?
John Forbes Nash Jr.: American mathematician and Nobel Laureate (1928–2015)
Born in Kabul to a diplomat, this Afghan-American physician-turned-novelist wrote the bestselling 'The Kite Runner' before serving as a UNHCR goodwill ambassador — who is he?
Khaled Hosseini: Afghan-American novelist (born 1965). Hosseini's novels have spread awareness about Afghanistan's people and culture.
He fathered the Ford Mustang in the 1960s, then rescued Chrysler from collapse as its CEO in the 1980s — one of the rare executives to run two of Detroit's Big Three. Who?
Nicknamed for the Greek goddess of wisdom, this roughly 22-centimeter nocturnal bird was introduced to Britain in the late 1800s and to New Zealand's South Island soon after — which species?
Little owl: Species of owl. It was introduced into Britain at the end of the 19th century and into the South Island of New Zealand in the early 20th century.
Developed by MathWorks and named for its focus on matrix manipulations, this proprietary numeric computing environment powers the add-on Simulink for model-based design. What's it called?
MATLAB: Numerical computing environment and programming language.

Studying under Rutherford at the Cavendish Lab, this Adelaide-born physicist discovered the nuclei of helium-3 and tritium and helped achieve the first experimental nuclear fusion — who was this Australian humanitarian?
Also nicknamed 'Cornish salmon,' this predatory fish is often netted alongside the Atlantic herring it preys on, and is heavily overfished across European waters — which fish?
Merluccius merluccius: Species of fish. Merluccius merluccius or the European hake is a merluccid hake of the genus Merluccius.

The only woman among Einstein's classmates at Zurich Polytechnic, this Serbian mathematician was his first wife and is still debated as a possible collaborator on his 1905 miracle-year papers. Who was she?
Mileva Marić: Wife of Albert Einstein (1875–1948)

This Japanese biologist used diffusion equations to calculate how likely a gene is to take over a population, and in 1968 proposed the "neutral theory" that genetic drift, not just selection, drives molecular evolution — who was he?
Also called the belly button, this flat or hollowed spot on the abdomen marks where the umbilical cord once attached — what is it?
Navel: Scarred area on the abdomen after detachment of the umbilical cord.

The first of the Century Series jet fighters, this supersonic aircraft was the U.S. Air Force's first fighter capable of level supersonic flight, first taking to the air in May 1953, seven months ahead of schedule — which jet?

North American F-100 Super Sabre: 1953 fighter aircraft family. The North American F-100 Super Sabre is an American supersonic jet fighter aircraft designed and produced by the aircraft manufacturer North American Aviation.

The world's most widespread and commercially important cactus species, this domesticated crop is grown both as a fruit and for its edible vegetable pads, likely originating in central Mexico — which species?
Opuntia ficus-indica: Species of cactus. It is grown primarily as a fruit crop, and also for the vegetable nopales and other uses.
Commonly known as the bullet ant for its notoriously painful sting, which insect species inhabits the humid lowland rainforests of Central and South America?
This serous membrane lines the abdominal cavity and serves as a conduit for the blood vessels and nerves of the organs it covers — what is it called?
Peritoneum: Membrane that forms lining of abdominal cavity or coelom.
Scientifically named Cajanus cajan, this perennial Fabaceae legume is a staple crop across the Indian subcontinent, Southeast Asia, Africa, and the Caribbean — what is it?
Pigeon pea: Species of perennial legume. The pigeon pea (Cajanus cajan) is a perennial legume from the family Fabaceae native to the Eastern Hemisphere.
Though they look like dolphins, these small toothed whales are actually closer kin to narwhals and belugas, with flat spade-shaped teeth instead of dolphins' cone-shaped ones — what are they called?
Porpoise: Small cetacean of the family Phocoenidae.

Found in more than 200 species of mushroom, this tryptamine alkaloid is itself biologically inactive — the body must dephosphorylate it into psilocin before the euphoria and time-bending kick in. What is it?
Psilocybin: Chemical compound found in some species of mushrooms.
This Indian social activist founded the Azadi Bachao Andolan and later teamed with yoga guru Ramdev to promote swadeshi economics — who was he?
Rajiv Dixit: Indian activist. Rajiv Dixit (30 November 1967 – 30 November 2010) was an Indian social activist who founded the Azadi Bachao Andolan.
Holding Oxford's inaugural chair for the Public Understanding of Science, which outspoken atheist and evolutionary biologist wrote 'The Selfish Gene'?
Richard Dawkins: British evolutionary biologist and author (born 1941)
This extinct armored jawless fish from the Ordovician period had closely-spaced eyes at the front of its head, 'like car headlamps,' and is best known from fossils found in Bolivia — what is it?
Sacabambaspis: Extinct genus of jawless fishes.
Distinguished from true seals by external ear flaps and the ability to walk on all fours, these marine mammals include a giant subspecies that can weigh up to 1,000 kilograms. What are they?
Sea lion: Subfamily of aquatic mammals.

No metal beats this one for electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity, or reflectivity, and it's mostly mined as a byproduct of refining copper, gold, lead, and zinc — which element, symbol Ag, is it?
Silver: Chemical element with atomic number 47 (Ag)
Native to the Andes, this is the only living species in South America from the short-faced lineage, and unlike most of its relatives, eats mostly plants — which animal?
Spectacled bear: Species of mammal. The spectacled bear (Tremarctos ornatus), also known as the Andean bear, is a species of bear native to the Andes Mountains in northern and western South America.

Named from Greek words meaning 'a chain of berries' and 'pus-forming,' this Gram-positive bacterial species is the predominant carrier of the Lancefield group A antigen, often abbreviated GAS — what is this bacterium's full scientific name?
Streptococcus pyogenes: Species of bacterium. The name group A (beta-hemolytic) Streptococcus is thus also used.
This orange citrus fruit is usually considered a mandarin variety, though it's also thought to carry some pomelo ancestry — which fruit?
First unearthed in Mongolia's Gobi Desert in 1948, this Late Cretaceous giant is known mainly from claw bones over half a meter long, giving it a name meaning 'scythe lizard' — which dinosaur genus?
Therizinosaurus: Therizinosaurid genus from the Late Cretaceous period.

Famous for oversized, colorful bills nearly useless for excavation, these Neotropical birds nest in hollows dug by other animals and share an ecological niche with Africa and Asia's hornbills — what are they?
Toucan: Family of birds. The family includes five genera and over 40 different species.
Made from strained yogurt mixed with cucumber, garlic, and herbs like dill or mint, this cold Greek dip is a classic topping for souvlaki and gyros — what is it called?
Tzatziki: Cold cucumber–yogurt dip, soup, or sauce.

The northernmost marsupial on Earth, this cat-sized nocturnal opportunist is a familiar visitor to trash cans and compost piles across North America, and often ends up as roadkill due to its slow pace — what is it?
Virginia opossum: Species of North American marsupial.
Aboard Apollo 8, the first crewed mission to leave low Earth orbit, this astronaut snapped the iconic "Earthrise" photograph as the crew circled the Moon ten times — who took it?
William Anders: American astronaut and lunar explorer (1933–2024)

The symbol for lanthanum is La. Lanthanum is a chemical element; it has symbol La and atomic number 57.
